headings: If You've Played Pandemic Legacy Season 1
What Stays and What Gets Reset?

sections.heading: Playing a Legacy Game
mechanicsSummary: Choices persist from game to game. Different groups get different campaigns.
Players will write on components, apply stickers to cards, characters, and the board, and sometimes tear up a card. Those changes are permanent.
Each game also ends with permanent upgrades chosen for later games.
Some material is sealed. Open a package or dossier only when an instruction says to.
Some rules are absent from the manual at the start. When found, those rules are stuck into the manual and replace what was there.

sections.heading: Legacy Deck
mechanicsSummary: 82-card story deck covering 12 months. Kept in a fixed order. Do not look through it or shuffle it.
During setup, read cards one at a time until a card whose back says PAUSE or STOP.
That card says when to resume: sometimes at the end of the current game, sometimes during setup of the next month.
The deck is one-way. Do not return Legacy cards when a month is replayed.
If the deck is scrambled, someone who is not playing restores the order from the number in each card's corner.

sections.heading: If You've Played Pandemic Legacy Season 1
mechanicsSummary: Shared ideas include the Legacy deck, rationing (called funding in Season 1), end-of-game upgrades, dossiers, and sealed packages.
Season 1 is not required. The two games are separate campaigns joined only by story.

sections.heading: What Stays and What Gets Reset?
mechanicsSummary: Permanent: writing, stickers on the board or cards, opening new material, scratching cards, and tearing up or destroying components.
When told to destroy a component, it never returns. Tear it up or set it aside.
Everything else resets at the start of each game, including pieces on the board, cards in hand, and incidents.

sections.heading: Game Months
mechanicsSummary: The campaign is 12 months, beginning in the 71st year after the end of the world.
A win advances the group to the next month.
The first loss of a month grants one retry of that same month, with the same rules and objectives. Set the lost game up again.
A second loss of that month still advances to the next month. The calendar does not wait.

sections.heading: End of the Campaign
mechanicsSummary: The campaign ends when December is finished, win or lose, and is then scored.
Score is mostly how many months were won. A win earlier in a month scores better than a win on the retry.
Grid population affects the score less than months won. Other criteria will add or subtract points.

sections.heading: The Prologue
mechanicsSummary: The prologue teaches rules that differ from base Pandemic and from Season 1.
The prologue has no legacy effects and no permanent changes.
Play it at least once, and repeat it as many times as the group wants, before starting the campaign.

sections.heading: Prologue Rules
mechanicsSummary: Two Prologue cards, found with the Player and Infection decks, walk through the objectives.
Read the Journal Entry / Prologue card for background and for which rules differ in the prologue.
Use the Prologue Objective card during the game.
